title: Build Your First Inventory
story:
You have joined the automation team at JumpToTech Bank. The team manages a fleet of servers, and every single thing they automate starts from the same place: a list of machines and how they are grouped.
Two web servers have just been handed to you — node1 and node2. Nobody has written them down anywhere yet, so as far as Ansible is concerned they do not exist. Your first job is to make Ansible aware of them, and prove it can actually reach them.
objectives: Explain what an Ansible inventory is and why groups matter
Write a static INI inventory containing a named host group
Read the parsed inventory back with ansible-inventory
Confirm real connectivity to managed nodes with the ping module

task.summary: Create an inventory containing a `web` group with node1 and node2, and prove Ansible can reach both.
task.description:
An inventory is Ansible's list of the machines it manages. In its simplest form it is a text file: host names, optionally arranged into groups. Groups are what let you later say "configure every web server" instead of naming machines one at a time.
Your project already contains an `ansible.cfg` that points at `inventory.ini`. That file does not exist yet — create it.
It must define a group called `web` containing two hosts, `node1` and `node2`. Those are the two managed nodes attached to your session. The connection details are already configured — `ansible.cfg` sets the remote user, and your control node already holds the session's SSH key — so the inventory itself is the only thing standing between you and a working `ansible web -m ping`.
Useful commands while you work:
`ansible-inventory --list` prints the inventory exactly as Ansible parsed it, which is the fastest way to see whether your file says what you think it says.
`ansible all -m ping` opens a real SSH connection to every host in the inventory and asks it to answer. A host that replies `pong` is genuinely reachable; nothing about it is simulated.

requirements: A 'web' group contains node1 and node2
Both web hosts answer ansible -m ping

hints.text: An inventory can be as simple as a few lines of text. Groups are declared with a header line, and the hosts belonging to that group are listed underneath it.

Read the "How to build your inventory" page in the official Ansible documentation. It shows the INI format your `ansible.cfg` is already expecting. After every edit, run `ansible-inventory --list` — if a host or a group is missing there, it is missing as far as Ansible is concerned.

The group must be named exactly `web` and must contain both `node1` and `node2`. Once `ansible-inventory --list` shows both hosts under that group, run `ansible web -m ping`. A host that answers SUCCESS is genuinely reachable; a host that answers UNREACHABLE is usually spelled differently in your file than it is in the fleet.
